steps: Choose one real production LLM project that you personally worked on and that you can discuss without exposing confidential details.
Write the problem and user/business goal in 3-5 sentences, including what made the problem hard.
Sketch the architecture: entry point, backend, model/provider, RAG or agent flow, storage, integrations, and observability.
Add concrete engineering evidence: latency, quality, retrieval metrics, failure rate, scale, or another measurement you actually observed.
Write three failure modes or difficult trade-offs and what you personally changed to handle them.
Compress the result into a one-page Markdown case that can be reused for interviews and a portfolio.
definition_of_done: A one-page production LLM case exists with a clear problem, architecture, model/RAG/agent flow, at least one real measurement, three failure modes or trade-offs, and an explicit description of your personal engineering decisions.

steps: Run lumen-radar and confirm that the top mission still matches current priorities.
Run lumen-work and inspect whether every step is concrete enough to execute without inventing missing context.
Complete one full work session and mark each finished step with lumen-work --done.
Write down one friction point that slowed the session and one capability that would remove it.
Turn the highest-value friction point into the next small Lumen experiment.
definition_of_done: One real work session has been completed through Lumen, progress is recorded locally, and at least one observed friction point has been converted into a concrete next experiment.

steps: Choose one robotics CI failure that can be detected locally and deterministically.
Define the rule contract: input, expected diagnostic, exit behavior, and false-positive boundary.
Add a minimal failing fixture that reproduces the problem.
Implement the rule and expose it through the existing RobotCI CLI path.
Add passing and failing tests plus a readable CLI-output assertion.
Document the rule with one copy-paste example in the README.
definition_of_done: RobotCI contains one end-to-end rule with a realistic failing fixture, deterministic diagnostic, green tests, CLI integration, and a README example.

steps: Freeze the current Elaine live stack for this acceptance run; do not add features during measurement.
Define the 25-interaction script and the exact success criterion for one interaction.
Run 25 consecutive voice interactions under the same environment and record every result.
Calculate completion rate, median end-to-end latency, and p95 latency.
Classify every miss into a concrete failure reason such as VAD, ASR, LLM, TTS, transport, or avatar playback.
Choose the single largest failure bucket as the next engineering target.
definition_of_done: A 25-interaction acceptance report exists with completion rate, median latency, p95 latency, a failure reason for every miss, and one evidence-backed next engineering target.
